newsitem.title: GERMANY: Stark says to recommend Bonn debt in euro in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Stark says to recommend Bonn debt in euro in 1999.

text.p: Juergen Stark, state secretary in the German finance ministry, said on Tuesday he would recommend to German Finance Minister Theo Waigel that the country's debt be converted into euro in 1999.
"I will propose to my finance minister that government debt should be converted to the euro in 1999," Stark said.
Stark was speaking at a news conference at the Bundesbank called to announce the issuance of a new strippable 30-year bond.
He also said Germany planned gradually to offer stripping of government debt across the full maturity curve.
The Bundesbank said earlier on Tuesday that it had sold 3.0 billion marks of the Bonn government's new 6.5 percent coupon 30-year bond via a consortium of banks.
The bond, sold at 99.75, had a yield of 6.52 percent, the Bundesbank said. The paper matures on July 4, 2027.
